slides.text: fib(30) makes 2,692,537 calls. fib(40) makes 331,160,281. In our test run (Python), fib(40) took 14.5 seconds.
slides.alt: "What does it cost?": fib(30) makes 2,692,537 calls; fib(40) makes 331,160,281 calls; 14.5 seconds in our Python test run.

slides.text: fib(3) runs twice, fib(2) three times, fib(1) five times. That's 15 calls to answer 6 different questions, and each repeat redoes its whole subtree: O(2ⁿ).
slides.alt: "fib(5): every call", tagged 15 calls · 6 questions and O(2ⁿ): the full call tree, 5 splitting into 4 and 3, down to leaves of 1 and 0, with the repeated calls in amber.

slides.text: The fix is to remember every answer:
slides.alt: The memoized fib(n, memo=None) in Python: create memo on the first call; if n < 2: return n; if n in memo: return memo[n]; memo[n] = fib(n - 1, memo) + fib(n - 2, memo), highlighted with the note "…store it, then return it"; the memo holds 2 → 1, 3 → 2, 4 → 3, 5 → 5: memo[5] = 5.

slides.text: Each value from 0 to n is computed once. fib(40) now takes 79 calls: O(n). In our test run it took 7 microseconds.
slides.alt: "Each value, once": fib(40), memoized, takes 79 calls, not 331,160,281: O(n). Naive fib(40) 14.5 s against memoized fib(40) 7 µs.

slides.text: One catch: it's still recursion. A memoized fib(1000) crashes Python with "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded".
slides.alt: "One catch: still recursion": every call is a stack frame. A memoized fib(1000) in Python raises RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded.

challenge: how many calls does the naive fib(6) make?
